source_rows.Authors: Schmidt JA, Huybrechts I, Overvad K, Eriksen AK, Tjønneland A, Kaaks R, Katzke V, Schulze MB, Pala V, Sacerdote C, Tumino R, Bueno-de-Mesquita B, Sánchez MJ, Huerta JM, Barricarte A, Amiano P, Agudo A, Bjartell A, Stocks T, Thysell E, Wennberg M, Weiderpass E, Travis RC, Key TJ, Perez-Cornago A

source_rows.comparison_type: Highest fifth versus lowest fifth of egg-protein intake

source_rows.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: protein and amino acid intakes were estimated using validated dietary questionnaires

sample_size.excerpt: In 131,425 men from the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, protein and amino acid intakes were estimated using validated dietary questionnaires.

cases.excerpt: During a mean follow-up of 14.2 years, 6939 men were diagnosed with prostate cancer and 914 died of the disease.

effect_size.excerpt: For prostate cancer death, we observed no strong associations with protein or amino acid intakes, but the results suggested that men who consumed more protein from eggs might be at a higher risk of dying from prostate cancer (Figure 2 and Table S4 ). The HRs (95% CIs) in the second to the top fifths compared to the lowest fifth were 1.09 (0.87, 1.36), 1.13 (0.90, 1.42), 1.07 (0.86, 1.34) and 1.22 (0.98, 1.53; p trend = 0.1), respectively.
effect_size.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

confidence_interval.excerpt: The HRs (95% CIs) in the second to the top fifths compared to the lowest fifth were 1.09 (0.87, 1.36), 1.13 (0.90, 1.42), 1.07 (0.86, 1.34) and 1.22 (0.98, 1.53; p trend = 0.1), respectively.
confidence_interval.location: Results, Risk of total prostate cancer and prostate cancer death

disease_scope_review.endpoint_excerpt: For egg protein intake and prostate cancer mortality, no association was observed by fifths, but there was suggestive evidence of a positive association in the analysis per standard deviation increment.
disease_scope_review.reason: The estimate concerns prostate cancer death during prospective cohort follow-up, representing a lethal prostate cancer endpoint rather than postdiagnosis survival analysis.

evidence_scope_projection.definition: Overall prostate cancer evidence, excluding estimates solely about aggressive prostate cancer. General estimates from papers that also report aggressive endpoints remain included. Uncertain endpoints retain their existing review and pooling restrictions.
